summary.en: Al-Shabaab continues assaults on Somali army positions in Lower Shabelle, killing a former al-Shabaab finance chief and adding to army casualties, while Somali forces have recaptured roughly half of territory previously held by al-Shabaab and ISIS. Uganda has begun pulling its troops after two decades and the African Union is withdrawing forces from four bases in Lower Shabelle, while Ethiopia is pulling more than 3,000 troops from Somalia as fighting intensifies at home. The UAE carried out its first drone strike against al-Shabaab in nearly a year. Somali pirates seized an Iranian fishing vessel and seven Pakistani crew members were rescued after a hijacking. The conflict caused 2,284 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Al-Shabaab fortsetter angrep på somaliske hærposisjoner i Nedre Shabelle, dreper en tidligere finanssjef i Al-Shabaab og øker antallet hærtap, mens somaliske styrker har gjenerobret omtrent halvparten av territoriet som tidligere var kontrollert av Al-Shabaab og IS. Uganda har begynt å trekke tilbake troppene etter to tiår, og Den afrikanske unionen trekker styrker fra fire baser i Nedre Shabelle, mens Etiopia trekker mer enn 3 000 soldater fra Somalia etter at kampene intensiveres hjemme. De forente arabiske emirater gjennomførte sitt første droneram mot Al-Shabaab på nesten ett år. Somaliske pirater kapret et iransk fiskefartøy, og syv pakistanske mannskap ble reddet etter kapringen. Konflikten forårsaket 2 284 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.extract: The ongoing phase of the Somali Civil War began in 2009 and is concentrated in southern and central Somalia, primarily between the forces of the Federal Government of Somalia (FGS), assisted by African Union peacekeeping forces, and the Islamist militant group al-Shabaab, which pledged allegiance to al-Qaeda in 2012.
